## Overview

This document replicates the news shock identification of @beaudry2014 . A news shock is identified as the shock that has **no contemporaneous effect on TFP** but **maximizes the long-run response of TFP** at a 40-quarter horizon. The approach follows the mixed restriction strategy combining a zero impact restriction with a long-run maximization criterion.

## Model and Identification

With $P$ the lower Cholesky factor of $\Sigma$, any rotation is observationally equivalent:

$$\Sigma = P P' = (P Q)(P Q)', \qquad Q Q' = I_K.$$

The news shock is the rotation vector $q$ orthogonal to the impact on TFP (variable 1) that maximizes the TFP response at the terminal horizon $H$:

$$q^{*} = \arg\max_{q\,:\,q'q = 1,\ (Pq)_1 = 0}
e_1'\Phi_H Pq,
\qquad H = 40,$$

where $e_1$ selects TFP. The impact vector is $b^{news} = P q^{*}$ and structural IRFs are $\Theta_h = \Phi_h P q^{*}$. Because $P$ is lower triangular, the zero-impact restriction $(Pq)_1=0$ is equivalent to setting the first element of $q$ to zero.

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(tictoc)
library(tidyMacro)

set.seed(12345)
set_theme(fThemeTidyMacro())
```
:::


## Data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data("BeaudryPortier2014")

y        <- BeaudryPortier2014 |> as.matrix()
T_obs    <- nrow(y)
N        <- ncol(y)
varnames <- colnames(y)
```
:::


## VAR Estimation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- 2
c <- 1

var_result <- fVAR(y, p = p, c = c)
Sigma <- var_result$sigma
```
:::


## News Shock Identification


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
horizon <- 40

# Wold IRFs by inverting (I - A(L))
wold <- fWoldIRF(var_result, horizon = horizon)

# Lower Cholesky factor of Sigma
S <- t(chol(Sigma))

# LR-Max point estimate
struct_irf <- fMaxIRF(wold, S, var_idx = 1L)
```
:::


## Bootstrap Confidence Bands


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tic()
boot_max <- fBootstrapMaxCorrected(
  y          = y,
  var_result = var_result,
  nboot1     = 1000,
  nboot2     = 2000,
  horizon    = horizon,
  var_idx    = 1,          # maximise long-run effect on TFP (variable 1)
  cumulate   = integer(0), # no cumulation (levels data)
  conf        = 90,         # Outer band
  conf2       = 68          # Inner band; matches the original replication
)
#> [Pass 1] Bias estimation: 1000 reps, 3 thread(s)
#> [Bias correction] 29 shrinkage iteration(s)
#> [Pass 2] Bias-corrected bootstrap: 2000 reps, 3 thread(s)
#> Using 3 thread(s) for LR-Max bootstrap...
toc()
#> 0.138 sec elapsed
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fPlotIRFLR(
  point       = struct_irf,
  boot_result = boot_max,
  varnames    = varnames,
  facet_ncol  = 2
) + labs(y  = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![IRF to Tech. news shock — LR-Max bootstrap (68% and 90% confidence bands)](02_2_Mixed_files/figure-html/fig-irf-boot-max-1.png){#fig-irf-boot-max width=100%}
:::
:::


## Compare the result to @barsky2012

Now we can compare the results to that of @barsky2012 and plot IRF results. This alternative chooses the zero-impact shock that maximizes the horizon-weighted cumulative contribution to TFP's forecast error variance, matching `uhlig_maxshare.m` in the replication files.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
struct_irf_uhlig <- fUhligIRF(wold, S, idx = 1L)

tic()
boot_uhlig <- fBootstrapUhligCorrected(
  y          = y,
  var_result = var_result,
  nboot1     = 1000,
  nboot2     = 2000,
  horizon    = horizon,
  idx        = 1L,        # maximise FEV share of TFP (variable 1)
  cumulate   = integer(0),
  conf        = 90,        # Outer band
  conf2       = 68         # Inner band; matches the original replication
)
#> [Pass 1] Bias estimation: 1000 reps, 2 thread(s)
#> [Bias correction] 34 shrinkage iteration(s)
#> [Pass 2] Bias-corrected bootstrap: 2000 reps, 2 thread(s)
#> Using 2 thread(s) for Uhlig max-share bootstrap...
toc()
#> 0.18 sec elapsed
```
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
fPlotIRFLR(
  point       = struct_irf_uhlig,
  boot_result = boot_uhlig,
  varnames    = varnames,
  facet_ncol  = 2
) + labs(y  = NULL)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![IRF to news shock — Uhlig max-share bootstrap (68% and 90% confidence bands)](02_2_Mixed_files/figure-html/fig-irf-boot-uhlig-1.png){#fig-irf-boot-uhlig width=100%}
:::
:::
